doc.title: Jimmy and Jeannie Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998

chapter: Power of music and big-band life
title: Favorite big bands and the bandstand experience
summary: Jimmy cannot pick a favorite big band; the bandstand where everything becomes one is the thing; Duke Ellington and Maynard Ferguson are mentioned.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Well said. Wow. Let me ask you about some things from years past. You had some big band experience along the way, with some of our more notable big band leaders.
If you had to pick a time that was one of your favorites in one of those bands, what might it be?
Well I can’t say favorites. Each one, in terms of the experience, what it offered me, was that same, like I say aspect of being uplifted.
There’s nothing like a big band.

And maintaining an open mind you see. Now sure I could talk about being on the road, and the negative hassles, and etcetera. But the amazing thing about it all, because you’re still sleeping and whatnot you know, and eating with the individuals, was on that bandstand.
Nothing like it. It’s worth everything.

Everything became one. And there’s all this diverse expression coming out of these horns. And from one section to the next, speaking to each other. Then in terms of mass unisons and you know, whatever, and solos, personal expression. And that whole band, just like when you hear Basie, it speaks.
And it was different when he was with Duke.
And Maynard Ferguson. I really liked hanging around with that group. They were really hip.
